title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Results, 'Contributions of single descending neuron types to steering behavior'; Figure 8A-C; Methods 'Stochastic ReaChR expression'
quote: In the flies with unilateral expression, we found that light evoked a small average steering bias in the ipsilateral direction
mapping_basis: The paper uses the Namiki/MANC type name DNa02; SS00730 maps to DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 617 nm orange light from above the head, symmetric on both sides, 68 uW/mm2 at the head, 0.5 s on every 11 s, 150 trials
type_coverage: stochastic: unilateral (one DNa02) or bilateral expression, scored post hoc by dissection
sensory_condition: on spherical treadmill (air-supported ball); head cuticle intact, no dissection before behaviour
penetrance: mean ipsilateral rotational velocity outside the 95% CI of a bootstrap null built from bilateral-expression siblings; individual flies varied (Fig. 8C)
n_flies_note: Fig. 8B legend: 16 unilateral / 17 bilateral flies; Methods: 9 left-only + 8 right-only = 17 unilateral and 47 bilateral of 73 experiments
notes: Flies were walking on the ball during illumination, so this is a steering bias in already-walking flies; leg-rhythm fields not_assessed per PROTOCOL 3, and no leg tracking was done. Forward-velocity changes were attributed to visual startle (indistinguishable across unilateral, bilateral and no-expression flies; data not shown), so they were not used. The bilateral-expression siblings served only as the null control for rotation, and the authors report no separate bilateral activation outcome, so no bilateral record was written. Off-target expression of SS00730 is from Figure 8-figure supplement 2 legend (shown with GtACR1/GFP). The 'simulation' in the text is a bootstrap resampling, not a connectome model. Other experiments in the paper are recordings, GtACR1 silencing, or CsChrimson in ORNs/thermoreceptors (not DNs), so none qualify.
